faq.q: How big was the Roman Empire?
faq.a: At its largest, around 117 CE, it stretched from Britain to Egypt and from Spain to Iraq, with perhaps 50 to 70 million people.

faq.q: Why did the Roman Empire split in two?
faq.a: It was too big for one ruler. Emperors shared power from the late 200s, and after Theodosius I died in 395 CE the East and West were ruled separately for good.
asks: When did Rome split into East and West?

faq.q: Why did Roman money lose value?
faq.a: Emperors needed cash for armies, so they mixed less silver into coins. People trusted the coins less and prices rose fast, which we call inflation.

faq.q: Who were the Goths and Vandals?
faq.a: Germanic peoples who moved into the empire, some as allies and soldiers, some as invaders. The Visigoths sacked Rome in 410 CE and the Vandals in 455 CE.

faq.q: Did the Roman Empire really end in 476?
faq.a: The Western empire did, when the general Odoacer removed the boy emperor Romulus Augustulus. The Eastern, or Byzantine, Empire lasted until 1453. Some historians call it a slow change rather than a sudden fall.
asks: When did the Roman Empire end?

facts: In 476 CE Odoacer removed Romulus Augustulus, the last Western Roman emperor.
The Visigoths sacked Rome in 410 CE.
The Eastern Roman Empire lasted until Constantinople fell in 1453.

quiz.say: When did the Western Roman Empire end?
quiz.show: The Western Roman Empire ended in…
quiz.why: In 476 CE the last Western emperor, Romulus Augustulus, was removed.

wrong.1: 1453 is when the Eastern empire's capital, Constantinople, fell.
wrong.2: 27 BCE is when Augustus became the first emperor.

quiz.say: Most historians say Rome fell because of…
quiz.show: Why did the Western empire fall?
quiz.why: Size, money troubles, civil wars and migrations all added up.

wrong.1: No single battle ended the empire.
wrong.2: Vesuvius buried Pompeii in 79 CE, but it did not end the empire.
